You can use the following code to add a GitHub issue in your repository:

```python
import requests

def add_github_issue(repo, title, body):
    api_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{repo}/issues"
    headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    data = {"title": title, "body": body}
    response = requests.post(api_url, headers=headers, json=data)
    return response.json()

repo = "your-repo-owner/your-repo-name"
title = "Your issue title"
body = "Your issue body"

issue = add_github_issue(repo, title, body)
print(issue)
```

This code will add a new issue to your repository with the provided title and body. Make sure to replace `YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN` with your actual GitHub token. 

You can also use the `requests` library to add a GitHub issue with more complex data structures, such as labels, milestones, and assignees. 

Remember to always handle errors and exceptions properly when making API requests. 

Also, you can use the `github` library, which is a Python wrapper for the GitHub API, to simplify the process:

```python
import github

g = github.Github("YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN")
repo = g.get_repo("your-repo-owner/your-repo-name")
issue = repo.create_issue(title="Your issue title", body="Your issue body")
print(issue)
```

Make sure to replace `YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN` with your actual GitHub token. 

This code will also add a new issue to your repository with the provided title and body.
